pageSummary:
Client background

Monadnock Media is an independent media organization serving the Monadnock region of New Hampshire with community-focused journalism. Founded in 2019, the organization publishes Monadnock Ledger-Transcript, a weekly newspaper covering local news, events and issues in the region. The team includes experienced journalists and editors committed to providing quality local journalism that serves the community's information needs.

Project goals and challenges

Monadnock Media needed a modern, flexible website that could support their journalism mission while providing an excellent user experience for readers. The team identified several key goals:

  • Create a headless CMS architecture. Build a Strapi-based content management system that would provide a robust backend for managing articles, authors, categories and multimedia content while enabling flexible front-end development.
  • Develop an engaging front-end experience. Work with design partner Aaron Taylor-Waldman to create a modern, responsive website that would showcase journalism effectively and provide an intuitive reading experience across devices.
  • Support advanced front-end development. Implement sophisticated animations, scroll-triggered effects and interactive elements that would enhance storytelling without compromising performance or accessibility.
  • Enable content management workflows. Provide editors and journalists with an intuitive interface for creating, editing and publishing content while maintaining editorial standards and brand consistency.
  • Optimize for performance and SEO. Ensure fast loading times, mobile responsiveness and search engine optimization to maximize reach and engagement with the community.

Approach

Headless CMS architecture with Strapi

The project began with implementing a Strapi headless CMS as the content management foundation. Strapi provided a flexible, API-first approach that would allow for sophisticated content modeling while enabling the front-end team to work independently. The CMS was configured with content types for articles, authors, categories, tags and multimedia assets, with custom fields and relationships to support the newspaper's editorial workflow.

Front-end development and animation prototyping

Knectar handled the front-end development, working closely with Aaron Taylor-Waldman's design vision to create a modern, engaging website. The development focused on advanced front-end techniques including scroll-triggered animations, quasi-3D layering effects and interactive elements that would enhance the reading experience. The team experimented with WebGL and p5.js for creating tactile, fluid interactions that would make the site feel more engaging and modern.

Scroll-triggered effects and interaction architecture

A key focus was implementing sophisticated scroll-triggered effects that would enhance storytelling without being distracting. This included techniques like scroll-triggered video/animation playback, parallax effects and dynamic content reveals that would engage readers as they moved through articles. The team used Svelte for implementing scroll triggers and other interactive elements, taking advantage of the framework's performance and developer experience.

Content management and editorial workflows

The Strapi CMS was configured to support the newspaper's editorial workflow, with user roles and permissions that matched the organization's structure. Editors could manage content through an intuitive interface, with features for scheduling publications, managing drafts and coordinating with the design team. The system also included tools for managing multimedia content, ensuring that images, videos and other assets were properly optimized and integrated into articles.

Performance optimization and responsive design

Performance was a critical consideration throughout development. The team implemented lazy loading for images and videos, optimized CSS and JavaScript delivery, and ensured that the site would load quickly across different devices and connection speeds. The responsive design was tested across various screen sizes to ensure an optimal reading experience for mobile, tablet and desktop users.

Outcomes

The new Monadnock Media website delivered a modern, engaging platform that successfully supported the organization's journalism mission. The headless CMS architecture provided the flexibility needed for both content management and front-end development, while the sophisticated animations and interactive elements created a more engaging reading experience that helped distinguish the publication in the competitive local media landscape.

The scroll-triggered effects and quasi-3D layering added visual interest without compromising the readability of articles, and the responsive design ensured that readers could access content effectively across all devices. The Strapi CMS streamlined editorial workflows, making it easier for journalists and editors to manage content while maintaining the publication's high editorial standards.

In summary

The Monadnock Media project demonstrated the value of combining a robust headless CMS with advanced front-end development techniques. By using Strapi for content management and implementing sophisticated animations and interactions, the team created a website that not only served the practical needs of a local newspaper but also provided an engaging, modern user experience that helped the publication stand out in the digital media landscape.
